disorder-name.detail: Early psychosis; the HCP-EP clinical cohort (91 individuals with early psychosis) was used to test whether normative brain regional Z-scores have an advantage over observed morphometric measures in predicting diagnostic status and symptom severity (PANSS psychosis score).
disorder-name.supporting_text: "We tested whether normative brain regional Z-scores have an advantage over the observed morphometric measures in predicting diagnostic status and symptom severity using psychosis as an example. [...] The HCP-EP cohort comprises 91 individuals with early psychosis and 57 healthy individuals (total sample 48 females and 100 males; age range 16·67-35·67 years)."
disorder-name.location: Ge2024.pdf.md: Methods / Relevance of normative models of brain morphometry for mental illness, L87-L89

dataset-of-origin.detail: Human Connectome Project - Early Psychosis Study. T1-weighted images were downloaded from the HCP repository and parcellated with FreeSurfer version 7.1.0.
dataset-of-origin.supporting_text: "we downloaded and parcellated (with FreeSurfer version 7.1.0) T1-weighted images from the repository of the Human Connectome Project-Early Psychosis Study (HCP-EP)."
